scope: Fixed development cache:30 roots,2 first16-control candidates, then the unchanged original-Goal fixed-seed native continuation. These are bounds on the recorded branch outcomes, not population or stochastic-environment guarantees.

prior_coverage.existing: The source already reports native/fixed/uniform utilities, two discordant-success roots and hindsight best-branch totals.
prior_coverage.incremental: This calculation adds explicit worst-branch totals and maximum possible first-choice damage against native or an unknown randomized scorer; no same-named prior bound artifact was found in the narrow report check. No new model or task evidence.

source_validation.raw_trace_audit: Reuse the existing independent branch audit; no repeated raw audit or hashes.

any_first_choice_selector.definition: Sum per-root min/max across the two recorded real continuation outcomes. Any stochastic selector is a convex combination within each root. Extremizers use hindsight outcome knowledge and are not feasible attacks.

relative_to_unknown_independent_finite_b.p_definition: p_r = P(independent scorer selects candidate1 at root r), including the declared score tie rule. No p_r or forecast bank has been measured here.
relative_to_unknown_independent_finite_b.baseline_success_expression: S_ind = sum_r [(1-p_r)*s_r0+p_r*s_r1]; for this cache S_ind=29-p_(task1,init2)+p_(task3,init2).
relative_to_unknown_independent_finite_b.success_loss_outer_bound_expression: S_ind-28; no more than2 expected successes across the panel without knowing S_ind.
relative_to_unknown_independent_finite_b.cost_increase_outer_bound_expression: 3646-C_ind; no more than416 total capped steps without knowing C_ind.
relative_to_unknown_independent_finite_b.coupling_limit: These are outer bounds for arbitrary first selectors. Keeping finite score-column marginals and using a restricted permutation can only narrow reachability; no unknown bank, selection probabilities, seed mixture or attainable permutation is invented. Independent forecast-column indices do not imply uniform candidate choice.

uniform_candidate_reference_separate.scope: Existing fair coin over the two candidate identities, not the unmeasured independent finite-bank scoring baseline.

decision.before_new_inference: Exclude any claim of three or more new failed roots, or losses across two tasks, relative to the recorded native controller under this first-choice-only design. Relative to any new randomized scorer, more than two lost successes is impossible on these stored branches.
decision.existing_first_choice_effect_already_rea: reports/cosmos_first_selection_mediation_20261015.json already derives29 native successes versus28 under the recorded Goal-Swap first choice using these same real continuations. Its one local loss reaches this cache's28-success floor; a different first-choice scorer cannot establish greater binary harm against the recorded native baseline here. This does not make the previous failed extension gate pass or establish a finite-bank operation.
decision.what_remains_testable: A bounded local or capped-step effect remains possible, but requires a pre-frozen operation blind to the real branch-utility table and a correctly labeled added stochastic scorer. Bounds alone give no attack signal.
decision.not_generalized: No claim about interventions at later decisions, different candidates, other roots, environmental repetitions, full closed-loop randomized planners or population ASR.

conditional_uniform_k4_coupling_bound.candidate_design_only: K4 is a proposed design condition, not a registered or executed Cosmos attack/scorer.
assumptions: Two fixed candidate identities, each with exactly four equally weighted scalar scores; hold the full bank, original action controls and real continuation utility fixed.
Selection uses fixed argmax with a candidate-identity tie rule independent of bank-row identities; original Cosmos ties select candidate0.
The reference chooses independent uniform column indices. The alternative joint law keeps both column-index marginals uniform; no score/action edits or utility-dependent bank selection.
Sort score rows/columns consistently; candidate1 winning cells form a Ferrers matrix, represented up to orientation by nondecreasing row counts in0..4.
conditional_uniform_k4_coupling_bound.extension_to_all_uniform_marginal_coupli: Any4x4 nonnegative joint table with row/column sums1/4 is a convex mixture of uniform permutation tables. Selection probability is linear in that table, so the permutation extrema bound all such couplings. This is a finite application of the doubly-stochastic matrix decomposition, not a new theorem.

cache_effect_bounds_relative_to_same_ban.formulas: success_loss <= choice_probability_bound*sum|s1-s0|; cost_increase <= choice_probability_bound*sum|c1-c0|. Also retain the tighter applicable support bounds S_ind-28 and3646-C_ind.
cache_effect_bounds_relative_to_same_ban.meaning: Bounds on expected aggregate utility, not maximum realized failures from one random row draw, nor a confidence bound.

limits: A global extremal Ferrers pattern need not occur in an actual Cosmos bank. The actual restricted permutation family may be weaker, and simultaneous per-root harm is not shown achievable without access to true utility.
This is relative to the independent uniform sampler on the same fixedK4 bank; it is not relative to native seed31/32 point-mass forecasts or the old deterministic native controller.
The bounds do not transfer unchanged to nonuniform bank weights, more than two candidates, row-dependent tie rules, changed scores, differentK, or repeated closed-loop interventions.
No forecast bank or attack output was generated; the only new computation is the1680-case mathematical enumeration.

reproduction: python scripts/analyze_cosmos_first_choice_bounds.py --verify-only; use --out <new-json-path> to write without overwriting. success_lower/upper=sum(min/max(s0,s1)); cost_lower/upper=sum(min/max(c0,c1)); subtract native totals or symbolic independent-scorer expectations. Standard-library JSON arithmetic only.
